bottleneck.description: MSS L/S-band spectrum and Band 53/n53 licenses underpinning Apple's iPhone Emergency SOS service; substitute D2D paths exist but lock-in is multi-year.

dependency.key_customers: Apple (anchor, ~85% capacity allocation), XCOM-Labs, Qualcomm, IoT and asset-tracking customers
dependency.key_suppliers: MDA Space (next-gen satellites), Rocket Lab (satellite bus subcontractor to MDA), SpaceX (launch)

editorial.notes: Globalstar has allocated 85% of current and future network capacity to Apple's Emergency SOS, with Apple investing ~$1.1B plus taking a ~20% equity stake to fund the next-generation constellation. The MSS spectrum (including Band 53/n53) and ground infrastructure are unique to Globalstar and not readily replicable. However, Apple could theoretically migrate to AST SpaceMobile, Iridium, or Starlink Direct-to-Cell over a multi-year horizon, so this is a costly but not impossible switch. Conservative MEDIUM in line with AST SpaceMobile-style D2C moats one tier above peers but below true sole-source.
